newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: ALPINE SKIING-PANZANINI CELEBRATES SECOND SEASON WIN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-PANZANINI CELEBRATES SECOND SEASON WIN.

text.p: Sabina Panzanini won her second victory of the World Cup season on Friday and attributed her success to weight loss.
Panzanini, who led an Italian one-two in a giant slalom, underwent special treatment at a clinic in the summer after doctors told her that recurring back problems were due to her being overweight.
The 24-year-old Panzanini, who won in Park City, Utah, in November, produced the quickest second run to improve on a first-leg fifth place for a winning aggregate time of two minutes 34.74.
First-run leader Deborah Compagnoni, the Olympic and world champion, shared second place with Austria's Anita Wachter in 2:34.82.

"It was nerve-wracking to be standing in the finish area watching Debbie come down. At first I thought she would win but in the end it was me," said a delighted Panzanini, who was often overshadowed by Compagnoni in the past.

"It was a great battle and a good slope. But I think Debbie can win here tommorrow," Panzanini said of Compagnoni, who captured her maiden slalom victory in Semmering, Austria, last weekend and is one of the favourites for Saturday's slalom here.
The Italian pair wrapped themselves in their national flag to pose for photographers in the finish area of the Pohorje piste in Slovenia's second largest city.
Panzanini's husband Michele -- whom she married in May -- was among the first to congratulate the winner on a snowy and foggy day with temperatures of minus five degrees Celsius.

Panzanini, from the northern Italian provincial town of Merano, began to suffer back pains soon after winning her first World Cup race, a giant slalom on the demanding slope at Alta Badia, Italy, in 1994.
At the time she weighed around 68 kgs but she slimmed down to around 63 kgs over the summer and has found a marked improvement in her form.
"I especially managed to improve my performance in the flatter parts of the slope where I used to previously lose so much time," Panzanini said on Friday.

Compagnoni, who also clinched super-G gold at the 1992 Olympic Games, was disappointed. "I'm a bit sad I couldn't keep my first leg lead but I am nevertheless happy for Sabina, she deserved this victory," Compagnoni said.
"In the second run, I made a big mistake in the upper part and then had problems with the fresh snow at the bottom," she added.
Sweden's Pernilla Wiberg retained the lead in the overall World Cup standings with 618 points -- ahead of title-holder Katja Seizinger of Germany on 534 -- despite finishing a poor 25th.
Wiberg, winner of the first of back-to-back slaloms in Semmering, hopes to perform better in Saturday's slalom.
Seizinger, winner of the season's opening giant slalom in Soelden in October, impressed with a fluid second run to improve from a first leg 14th place to overall sixth.
The 24-year-old German is tied with Panzanini in the giant slalom standings on 200 points after three races.
Slovenian Urska Hrovat, third after the first run, disappointed home crowds by failing to make the podium. She finished fourth in 2:35.23.
